title: Middle school physics: forces and balance
description: Four lessons from net force to balanced structures: predict, manipulate a balance micro-world, and transfer to bridges and tug-of-war.
assumptions: Forces are whole-number newtons on a line; balance means equal opposing pulls. No real apparatus or network needed.
stage1goal: Build the net-force idea from evidence.
stage2goal: Explain balance and use it in new structures.
net-force.title: Net force: add with direction
net-force.goal: Compute net force on a line and predict motion change.
net-force.reading: Forces on a line add with direction: opposite pulls subtract. Zero net force means no change in motion.
net-force.worked.prompt: In your own words: what does zero net force mean?
net-force.worked.fb: No change in motion: rest stays rest, moving keeps moving.
net-force.worked.content: Left pull 5 N and right pull 5 N on a box: net 0, the box keeps doing what it did.
net-force.compute.prompt: Left 12 N, right 5 N. What is the net force magnitude?
net-force.independent.prompt: Net force is zero. The box is moving. What happens?
net-force.independent.fb: It keeps moving at the same speed.
net-force.independent.hint: Zero net force means no change.
net-force.independent.a.label: It stops immediately
net-force.independent.b.label: It keeps moving unchanged
net-force.c1.a.label: Net force zero
net-force.c1.b.label: No forces act
balance-lab.title: Balance micro-world
balance-lab.goal: Manipulate both pans and observe balance and difference.
balance-lab.reading: The balance tips toward the heavier pan; the difference tells how much. Equal pans balance.
balance-lab.worked.prompt: Why does the pan with 7 g against 3 g tip?
balance-lab.worked.content: Left 7 g, right 3 g: difference 4 g, tips left.
balance-lab.balance.prompt: Left pan holds 9 g. What must the right hold to balance?
balance-lab.independent.prompt: Raise right to 12 while left stays 9. Which way tips?
balance-lab.independent.a.label: Left
balance-lab.independent.b.label: Right
balance-lab.c1.b.fb: That is the sum, not difference.
tug-of-war.title: Tug-of-war and bridges
tug-of-war.goal: Explain balance in teams and structures using net force.
tug-of-war.reading: A structure stands when every part has zero net force; a rope moves toward the larger total pull.
tug-of-war.struggle: Two teams pull a rope and it does not move. Without numbers, explain what must be true about their pulls.
tug-of-war.worked.prompt: What does the unmoving rope tell you about the two pulls?
tug-of-war.worked.fb: They are equal and opposite: net zero.
tug-of-war.worked.content: Team A 400 N left, team B 400 N right: rope stays.
tug-of-war.independent.prompt: Team A adds one puller (+80 N). What happens to the rope?
tug-of-war.independent.fb: Moves toward A: net 80 N left.
tug-of-war.independent.a.label: Moves toward A
tug-of-war.independent.b.label: Stays still
tug-of-war.transfer-bridge.prompt: A bridge deck weighs 900 N down. Two cables share the load equally. How many newtons up does each cable pull?
tug-of-war.transfer-bridge.hint: Total up must equal total down.
tug-of-war.c1.a.label: No forces on it
tug-of-war.c1.b.label: Zero net force on each part
explain-to-engineer.title: Explain balance to an engineer
explain-to-engineer.goal: Teach the balance rule clearly enough to check a structure.
explain-to-engineer.reading: A good explanation states zero-net-force, gives one example, and names the unbalanced case.
explain-to-engineer.worked.prompt: Say the balance rule in one sentence.
explain-to-engineer.worked.fb: Every part keeps its motion when its net force is zero.
explain-to-engineer.worked.content: Rule: zero net force. Example: 400 N vs 400 N rope. Unbalanced: 480 N vs 400 N moves.
explain-to-engineer.teach-check.prompt: Explain to a friend why a book on a table does not fall through.
explain-to-engineer.teach-check.fb: The table pushes up with a force equal to the book weight: net zero.
explain-to-engineer.teach-check.content: A good explanation names both forces and their equality.
explain-to-engineer.transfer-elevator.pr: New situation: an elevator cable pulls up 5000 N while the cab weighs 5000 N. What does the cab do?
explain-to-engineer.transfer-elevator.fb: Keeps its current motion (rest or steady speed).
Net zero also allows steady motion.
explain-to-engineer.c1.a.label: Only rest
explain-to-engineer.c1.b.label: Rest or steady motion
explain-to-engineer.c2.prompt: Two equal cables hold 900 N. Each pulls…
explain-to-engineer.c2.a.label: 450 N
explain-to-engineer.c2.b.label: 900 N
